item.title: Re: Crimes Against Nature
item.content:encoded: Thanks for the idea! I'll try to expand upon this as much as I can!

item.title: Re: Crimes Against Nature
item.content:encoded: I like the overall idea, it has the same vibe as some other "alien" SCPs but it has its own way of doing that, and I think this idea has a lot of potential. However, I think that it would be wise to narrow your scope a bit. For example, what specific kind of beast do those that violate the laws turn into (I think something resembling a Lamassu could be intriguing)? Why was it specifically made by non-humans, and does this have any bearing on what it does or says specifically? I also feel that, though perhaps a bit obvious, exploring the connection with the Ten Commandments could be interesting. As I said before, I really like the idea you've got here, but spend a bit more time on hammering out a cohesive storyline and connections. Good luck with your writings! :D

item.title: Crimes Against Nature
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type:SCP

Genre (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A 12 in. stone tablet that has a set of ten laws written in cuneiform, supposedly connected to the biblical ten commandments and a theoretical God. Breaking these laws will transform the offender into a nightmarish and deformed cannibalistic beast,resembling the celestial entity from ancient mesopotamian mythos,the Lamassu within a 100km radius. Though children don't seem to be affected. The foundation speculates this is due to the fact children didn't participate in a war, shown on hieroglyphics near the tablet.

Central Narrative: The tablet is found by two miners below hieroglyphics of a war between humanoid entities(Which appeared to be hybrids between humans and various animals, including llama's,lions,cats, etc.) and what appears to be an angel descending into a pyre. The next day their remains were found next to the tablet.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The tablet seems to have been created by something non-human (known because the figure holding it on the walls is clearly non-human, however what it is isn't clear) as a sort of declaration of independence, but by what? And why?
